requirements.title: Procedure reference establishes dummy-to-effective argument association
requirements.definition: Execution of a procedure reference establishes correspondence between each actual argument and dummy argument and association between each present dummy argument and its effective argument; sequence association is one form of argument association.

pending.procedure-reference-establishes-argument: Existing owner doc/catalogues/argument_association_15_5_2_4.json (S15.5.2.4-006) supplies the procedure-reference association rule: call subroutine set_to_42(x) with host integer actual initialized to 1 and dummy d assigned 42; exact post-call x=42 proves association rather than a local copy.
pending.present-dummy-associated-with-effective-: Existing owners doc/catalogues/argument_correspondence_15_5_2_1.json and doc/catalogues/argument_association_15_5_2_4.json supply correspondence/effective-argument rules: pass actuals initialized to 1 and -7 to two dummy names and mutate only the present dummy; exact final values distinguish present association from absent/default state.
pending.sequence-association-cross-reference: Existing owner doc/catalogues/sequence_association_15_5_2_12.json covers sequence association; this source entry records the cross-reference only and adds no duplicate fixture.

requirements.title: Dummy argument name is the procedure-local access name for the effective argument
requirements.definition: A dummy argument name may differ from the effective argument name. The dummy argument name is the name by which the effective argument is known and accessed in the referenced procedure.

pending.dummy-name-may-differ: Existing owner doc/catalogues/argument_association_15_5_2_4.json (S15.5.2.4-006) supplies the dummy/effective-argument association: call subroutine rename_probe(formal) with actual actual_value initialized to 1; assigning formal=42 yields exact actual_value=42 despite distinct names.
pending.dummy-name-accesses-effective-argument: Existing owner doc/catalogues/argument_association_15_5_2_4.json supplies the effective-argument access rule: a host variable formal is initialized to -777 and actual actual_value to 1; inside the procedure dummy formal=42 changes actual_value, leaving the host homonym unchanged.

requirements.title: Argument associations from one procedure reference terminate at return and new invocations can associate different effective arguments
requirements.definition: Upon termination of a procedure reference, all argument associations established by that reference terminate. A dummy argument can be associated with a different effective argument in a later invocation.

pending.argument-association-terminates-on-retur: Existing owner doc/catalogues/argument_association_15_5_2_4.json supplies the invocation association rule; this 19.5.1.2 plan calls set_dummy(a,42) then set_dummy(b,77) with a=1 and b=2, expecting exact a=42 and b=77 so the first association cannot persist.
pending.subsequent-invocation-new-effective-argu: Existing owner doc/catalogues/argument_association_15_5_2_4.json supplies the invocation association rule; this 19.5.1.2 plan uses a single dummy name d with distinct actuals a,b and observes writes 42 then 77 to different variables, exposing stale-association errors.
